rubric_items.reason: SY-1 and SY-2 restate the actual result, the expected result and both acceptance criteria, each with a ticket line cite (L13-L14, L20-L21, L24-L26).
Both candidates are module-map symbols with cites. The link from PatientsPage to the patient list is an inference from the name and path (A-1), stated openly; the page code itself was not read.

The page is ranked high because the symptom is how an empty value is displayed. The API is ranked low because it would only be the cause if it sent the literal 'None'. Both reasons follow from the evidence.

The checks are specific: find the no-next-appointment branch of the cell in PatientsPage.tsx and confirm it renders 'None', and confirm what GET /api/patients returns. Each check confirms or rules out a candidate.
The assumption A-1 and the unknown U-1 are stated as such. However, U-1's resolution path (reading the page code) does not actually show what the API sends.

findings.text: U-1 asks what the API sends for an empty next appointment, but says reading the page code settles it. Page code cannot show the API payload. Candidate 2's next check (inspect the GET /api/patients item) is the right way to settle it.
